Implementation Plan

The work is just two files under `analysis/`: delete the processed source doc and append its entry to the processing report. All four implementation changes are on `orchestrator/project-7614`, so the four "applied" verdicts stay as the issue states them, with no deferrals.

## Plan: report entry and source-doc cleanup for `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-2.md` (Refs #7614)

**Planning ref:** `orchestrator/project-7614` at `3d0ca137ccf7eb3b527518d1d590ef58f0d4e8f4`. Integration branch mismatch: false.

### Automation-bias summary (§20.E)
- **Scripts:** this change adds no script and changes none. It only edits files under `analysis/`.
- **Scheduler entry point:** none. The change is a one-time cleanup in the project's final PR. A side effect: once the doc's basename is in the report, the promote cycle (`scripts/apply_analysis_on_main.sh`, line 328, `grep -qF` on the basename) will not dispatch this doc again.
- **Supervisor:** none needed.
- **Database work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry needed.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md
Scope-mode justification: The issue names exactly two edits: delete the doc and append one entry to the report. The four implementation issues have already landed on the integration branch, which I checked:
- `REVIEWER_PASS2_SHADOW` and `usage_missing_reason` are in `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`.
- `PROMOTE_CYCLE_FAILED ... failed_job=... failed_step=...` is in `scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh`.
- `stderr_category` is in the committed `scripts/memory_helpers.sh` (`git show HEAD:` finds 4 occurrences).
- The fragments `changelog.d/7625-reviewer-pass2-shadow.md`, `7614-reviewer-usage-missing-reason.md`, `7614-promote-gate-failure-linkage.md` and `7615-memory-fail-open-telemetry.md` are present.

So the verdicts listed in the issue can be written as given. The entry reuses the format of the existing per-doc entries (heading, then `Processed:`, then one bullet per verdict). Nothing beyond that is in scope.

## Files likely to change
- `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-2.md`
- `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`

## Functions or modules to implement
None. This is a documentation and data-file change only.

1. **Delete the source doc.** Run `git rm analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-2.md`. The implementer does not need to read it: every verdict is spelled out in the issue body.
2. **Update the processed-docs list** in `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`:
   - Change the heading on line 5 from `## Processed source docs (122)` to `## Processed source docs (123)`. The list currently has exactly 122 `` - `analysis/...` `` bullets, so the new count is consistent.
   - Insert `` - `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-2.md` `` directly after the last bullet, `` - `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21.md` `` (line 129), and before the blank line that precedes `## Downstream local issue ID recheck`.
   - Make no other changes to that list or anywhere else in the file.
3. **Append the per-doc entry** at the end of the file, after the `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21.md` entry (the file currently ends at line 1253). Leave one blank line, then add:
   - the heading ``### `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-2.md` ``
   - the line `Processed: <UTC date of the PR>`. Use `date -u +%F`; today that gives 2026-10-18.
   - one `- <Recommendation> — <verdict>: <reason>` bullet per item, in the order the issue lists them. Use the same em-dash style as the 2026-09-21 entry.

**Bullet text to use.** Keep the issue's facts. Cite the changelog fragment for each applied item, as the 2026-09-21 entry does.
- Speed 1 / Reliability 2 first half (early CI budget-contract fail-fast) — already-implemented: CI has run as parallel jobs since #4707. The `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py` contract runs at the start of each orchestrate-poll group. The `300 != 180` mismatch is fixed on main.
- Speed 2 (adaptive second review pass) — applied as shadow-only: reviewer-pass2-shadow (`changelog.d/7625-reviewer-pass2-shadow.md`). `REVIEWER_PASS2_SHADOW` logs `would_skip` after pass 1. Pass 2 always runs, following the doc's own rollout advice.
- Speed 3 (reject superseded heads before model startup) — already-implemented, and its unsafe part rejected:
  - The gate checks out the authenticated current PR head (`review_checkout_sha`).
  - `AUTOFIX_STALE_BASE_SKIP` covers heads that advance during fetch.
  - Skipping a run whose event head moved would leave the newest head unreviewed when that head is a self-triggered `[ai-autofix]` push whose own synchronize run is skipped.
- Speed 4 (short-circuit idle polls) — already-implemented: ticks with no project run only the sweep-only modes (`has_work=false`). Ticks with active projects cannot be short-circuited safely.
- Cost 1 (adaptive model fan-out) — already-implemented by the lite/standard/full review tiers and the risk-tier resolver.
- Cost 2 (enable uninteresting-file filtering) — rejected: the doc requires a shadow comparison first, and no shadow mode exists. Operators can opt in with `REVIEWER_FILTER_UNINTERESTING_ENABLED`.
- Cost 3 (instrument Semble usefulness) — already-implemented: `SEMBLE_QUERY` logs bytes, ms, sources and static_dup_bytes.
- Cost 4 (usage completeness) — applied: reviewer-usage-missing-reason (`changelog.d/7614-reviewer-usage-missing-reason.md`). `usage_missing_reason` is added to the reviewer usage line.
- Reliability 1 (required review env manifest) — already-implemented: `LINKED_ISSUE_METADATA_FILE` is set, and `REVIEW_EDITOR_PREFLIGHT` checks the editor guards before the reviewers run.
- Reliability 2 second half (release child-run linkage) — applied: promote-gate-failure-linkage (`changelog.d/7614-promote-gate-failure-linkage.md`). `PROMOTE_CYCLE_FAILED` now names the failed job and step.
- Reliability 3 (cancellation diagnostics) — rejected: runs cancelled before their first step cannot log, and those cancellations are the concurrency group's normal replacement of a pending run.
- Reliability 4 (opaque AI-memory fail-open events) — applied: memory-fail-open-telemetry (`changelog.d/7615-memory-fail-open-telemetry.md`). Adds `exit_code`, `duration_ms` and `stderr_category`.
- Reliability 5 (MCP fallback alert threshold) — rejected: there is no fallback-rate alert to retune.
- GH API audit (reuse the linked-issue snapshot after merge) — already-implemented: `POST_MERGE_LINKED_ISSUES_JSON` is reused and refreshed only when empty, and `post_merge_validate_context_definitely_empty` skips the job.
- GH API audit (per-request `GH_API_CALL` logging) — rejected as broad scope: `GH_API_RETRY` and `GH_PAT_BUDGET` already cover failures and quota.
- Prompt cache 1 (stable prefix) — already-implemented.
- Prompt cache 2 (prefix_hash telemetry) — rejected as broad scope.
- Prompt cache 3 (filtering/dedup) — see Cost 2 and Cost 3.
- Prompt cache 4 (automatic context reduction at 70%) — rejected: it changes behaviour with a quality risk. `CONTEXT_BUDGET_WARN` remains.
- AI memory budget target of 80–90% — rejected as speculative tuning.
- `ORCHESTRATOR_CYCLE_SUMMARY` and the merge-train blocker-age metric — rejected for now: they would add instrumentation to the hot poller script, and `POLL_PROGRESS`, `GH_PAT_BUDGET` and `STANDALONE_STALL_PROBE` already provide part of this.
- Clarify/plan structured skip reasons — already-implemented (`AI_PHASE_GATE_V1`).

If the fragments have already been folded by the time the PR is written, use "(fragment folded into `CHANGELOG.md`)" instead of the path. That is the existing precedent in the 2026-09-21 entry.

## Data structures affected
`analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` gets two insertions: one bullet in the processed-docs list and one new section at the end of the file. The count in the line-5 heading changes from 122 to 123. No existing content is reflowed, renumbered or removed.

## API or interface changes
None. One downstream effect: `scripts/apply_analysis_on_main.sh` finds the basename in the report with a `grep -qF` substring match, so it will skip this doc from now on, and the doc is deleted in the same PR.

## Decisions
### D1 — Placement of the new entry
- Chosen: append the entry at the end of the file, directly after the `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21.md` entry, using the same `### ` heading, `Processed:` line and bullet layout.
- Alternatives considered: create a new "Outcome ledger for …" `##` section; insert the entry in date order somewhere earlier in the file.
- Why: the most recent per-doc entries (2026-09-16 through 2026-09-21) are appended at the end without a new `##` wrapper. Appending keeps the change append-only and avoids reflowing anything, as the issue requires.

### D2 — No changelog fragment
- Chosen: add no `changelog.d/` fragment for this PR.
- Alternatives considered: add a fragment describing the cleanup.
- Why: the change only touches `analysis/` triage data, which the release pipeline does not count as a code change. The earlier report and cleanup PR for 2026-09-21 added no fragment, and the issue limits this PR to the two files.

### D3 — Verdicts for the four implementation issues
- Chosen: record Speed 2, Cost 4, Reliability 2 (second half) and Reliability 4 as applied, each citing its fragment.
- Alternatives considered: record them as deferred, as the issue says to do for any implementation issue that did not merge.
- Why: all four are on the integration branch's committed `HEAD` (checked above). Note that the planning sandbox's working copy of `scripts/memory_helpers.sh` shows `main`'s staged support copy. The committed blob has the change.

- **Trust boundaries:** none crossed. No automation path (`scripts/`, `.github/`, `prompts/`, `.claude/`, `workflow-templates/`) is touched, so the automation-path
